steps: Metals lose their outermost electrons easily.
items.finalAnswer: Metals lose outer electrons easily, while non-metals gain electrons easily.

steps: Lower molecular mass covalent compounds have weak forces of attraction between their molecules.
Only a small amount of energy is needed to overcome these forces, so they exist as gases or low-boiling liquids.
items.finalAnswer: Weak intermolecular forces make lower molecular mass covalent compounds gases or low-boiling liquids.

steps: Diamond is an element that exists as a crystalline solid.
Its carbon atoms are joined by covalent bonds.
items.finalAnswer: Diamond is a crystalline solid with covalent bonds between its carbon atoms.

steps: The layers of metal atoms can slide over one another when a force is applied.
This property makes metals malleable and ductile.
items.finalAnswer: The ability of layers of metal atoms to slide over one another makes metals malleable and ductile.

steps: Yes. A coordinate covalent bond, once formed, is as strong as an ordinary covalent bond.
items.finalAnswer: Yes, a coordinate covalent bond is as strong as an ordinary covalent bond.

steps: Place N in the centre and arrange three O atoms around it; attach H to one O to form the –OH group.
Join N to the –OH oxygen by a single covalent bond and to a second oxygen by a double covalent bond.
Show the third oxygen donating a lone pair to N with a coordinate bond, O→N.
Use dots and crosses to distinguish the electrons from different atoms, and show the lone pairs on the oxygen atoms.
items.finalAnswer: The dot-and-cross formula has an –OH group, an N=O double bond and an O→N coordinate bond.

steps: HF molecules form hydrogen bonds with one another because fluorine is highly electronegative.
These intermolecular attractions are strong, so more energy is needed to separate HF molecules.
HCl molecules do not form hydrogen bonds and have weaker intermolecular attractions; therefore, HCl is a gas while HF is a liquid.
items.finalAnswer: Hydrogen bonding between HF molecules makes HF a liquid, while HCl has weaker intermolecular forces and is a gas.

steps: Water is a polar solvent, whereas most covalent compounds are non-polar.
Because of this difference, most covalent compounds do not dissolve in water.
items.finalAnswer: Most covalent compounds are non-polar, so they are generally not soluble in polar water.
